$comment: ONE artifact, THREE consumers. Two independent fixtures in two modules is
exactly how the drift this file exists to prevent happened: the worker sent
source_event as a string and omitted org_id, the gateway required a dict and
a non-null string, every write 422'd for months, and both suites stayed green
because each asserted its own side's assumption.
and that every entry in rejected_variants is REJECTED
If you change the gateway schema, this file must change, and the worker/TS
tests fail until their builders follow. That is the point — do not fork it.

rejected_variants.name: source_event_as_string
rejected_variants.why: The original bug (worker sent the literal string 'worker:entrypoint'). source_event is JSONB NOT NULL and the schema requires an object; a string must 422 so a revert cannot pass silently.

rejected_variants.name: org_id_null
rejected_variants.why: The second, independent cause of the same 422. action_provenance.org_id is VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL (migration 016), so a null must be rejected at the schema boundary rather than reaching the DB as a 500.

rejected_variants.name: org_id_missing
rejected_variants.why: Omitting the key entirely must fail the same way as sending null — the worker previously never passed org_id at all.

response.$comment: The gateway returns CreateProvenanceResponse: {id, created_at}. It has NEVER returned 'provenance_id' — the old client read that key, and the old tests mocked it, which is why the latent third bug was invisible.
